extracted.intended_audience: prospective journalism students (high school, undergraduate, and graduate) and their families
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of Medill School of Journalism programs, opportunities, and faculty expertise designed to prepare students for careers in journalism and media through coursework, labs, global experiences, and industry mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enduring journalism skills and values
rubrics_metrics.description: "We combine the rigors of a top-10 research university with enduring journalism skills and values and technology expertise essential for you to thrive in today's media landscape."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames mastery of core journalistic practice and professional ethics as a central program outcome, integrated with academic rigor and technological competence. Implies evaluation of students on foundational reporting, accuracy, ethics, and critical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology expertise / digital media strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Knight Lab allows you to better understand how technology changes the way we report, consume and share news and information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes ability to use and understand new tools, platforms, and digital distribution/revenue strategies. Faculty focus (e.g., Knight Professor in Digital Media Strategy) suggests assessing proficiency in digital storytelling, analytics, platform strategy, and product-minded journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative journalism experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "Undergraduate and graduate students in the Medill Investigative Lab work side-by-side with veteran journalists on an investigation of national importance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes hands-on investigative skills, collaboration with experienced journalists, and engagement on high-impact, real-world investigations. Implies criteria such as source development, data analysis, legal/ethical vetting, and sustained reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-platform storytelling and video/broadcast specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty profile: faculty lead video and broadcast specialization and are described as "specializing in multi-platform storytelling and solo journalism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values competency across formats (video, broadcast, online) and the ability to tell stories across multiple platforms. Assessment would include production skills, visual storytelling, editing, and ability to adapt stories for different media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and writing proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty teach core courses in reporting and writing (e.g., "Elise De Los Santos teaches undergraduate and graduate classes on reporting and writing").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions strong reporting and clear writing as fundamental; evaluation likely covers news judgment, sourcing, clarity, structure, accuracy, and ability to write for different beats and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global journalism experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "We offer a variety of week-long global trips, chances to work in professional media outlets abroad and quarter-long opportunities to study abroad."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages exposure to international reporting and cross-cultural journalism practice. Criteria include ability to report in different cultural contexts, adaptability, understanding of global issues, and experience working with international newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking and professional connections
rubrics_metrics.description: "Network with industry professionals and meet Medill students and faculty." (Alumni examples and career placements are highlighted.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values building professional relationships and leveraging alumni/faculty networks for career development. Assessment of student success may include internships, placements, and professional mentorship engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential learning through labs, programs, and fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs highlighted include Knight Lab, Medill Investigative Lab, Medill Explores, and fellowships/workshops (e.g., George R.R. Martin Summer Intensive Writing Workshop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes applied learning opportunities outside traditional classes — short immersions, semester projects, and fellowships. Suggests evaluation based on project-based outcomes, real-world reporting experience, and participation in institutional labs or academies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty real-world expertise and specialized mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty bios stress professional backgrounds (e.g., former national correspondents, editors, documentary filmmakers, journalists who are also lawyers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that student training is informed by practitioner experience; implies criteria such as mentorship quality, access to industry knowledge, and specialty-driven instruction (sports journalism, politics, investigative, law-related reporting).
